questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The sunny climate and the close proximity to beautiful nature and famous cities such as Los Angeles and San Fransisco.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information was very accessible. The only major problem concerned transportation. I had expected to buy a used car upon arrival. However, upon arrival and after a lot of research I found that this required first obtaining a Californian driver's license. I ended up long-term-renting a car instead from the rental company recommended by the university. This ended up being a good experience. However, because I had not ordered a rental car in advance, I only got a rental car after several weeks. The limited availability of public transportation in San Diego meant that the first two weeks was a bit boring and troublesome, and felt a bit wasted.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange staff at USD were friendly and offered their help when necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I ended up finding housing through Airbnb. Housing was extremely expensive but other than that it was good.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My first rental was east of downtown in Sherman Heights. As this was close to downtown I expected this to be a vibrant neighborhood. However, it was more of a ghetto vibe with some homeless people, and it was far from all the cozy neighborhoods of San Diego. My advice would be to research on the specific areas before deciding where to live. Specifically for San Diego I would prioritize living close to the sea or in North Park.

questions.answer: Course registration went smoothly and the guidance on courses were helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I talked to a supervisor while registrating for courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would prioritize registrating for courses with classes on the same days so that you have a long weekend to travel. I had all my courses on Monday and Wednesday. This meant that I could leave on a roadtrip for San Fransisco or Utah on a Wednesday evening a only get back Sunday without missing any classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level of the courses and the examination quite easy. To me the UCPH requirement that you must be a Master's student with a GPA of at least 7 on the Danish scale in order to even apply for the University of San Diego seems very unnecessary. The classes were easy to follow as a person with good command of English, and a lot of exchange students from other countries displayed a level in English and in law that was way below a typical danish level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers were generally very kind and knowledgeable and I learned a lot. We were told that the socratic method would be used a lot. However, this wasn't the case. Thus, it resembled the teaching style at UCPH a lot. However, the teachers generally spend more time talking about irrelevant subjects such as their academic accolades or telling stories with no or little legal educational content. Slashing these irrelevant subjects, the classes could probably have been generally 30-minutes shorter while still providing the same education.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Negotiation
Intro to U.S. law
International Energy Law
Corp Innovation and Legal Policy
Legal Writing and Research (GRAD)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all of the courses.

Negotiation, Intro to U.S. law, and Legal Writing and Research (GRAD) all had very easy forms of examination which was particularly nice as an exchange student.

For International Energy Law, and Corp Innovation and Legal Policy I had to hand in a paper of about 15-20 pages including footnotes. I had written several papers in English on my Bachelor's and Master's in UCPH already to this turned out to be easy as well. But you should consider whether you want to write to papers during your semester or not.

All of the classes concerned subjects that are useful in a Danish context as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It seemed like there was a lot of good opportunities. However, I made some friends outside of USD who I played beachvolleyball and basketball with instead.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different team sports. Watching sports such as basketball and football.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend roadtripping in the weekend, trying surfing, watching basketball games at USD.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nature such as Yosemite, Sequoia and Kings Canyon, Zion, Bryce Canyon (all before winter sets in around November). Antelope canyon, Grand Canyon, Death Valley. San Fransisco, Big Sur, Los Angeles, Hawaii. Attend an NBA game in LA.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Minor differences but overall it was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Prepare for U.S. citizens being very open and use this openness to make some friends. I have played some basketball and beach volleyball in Denmark and used these hobbies to connect with people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: All our friends would go to bed very early, so we often didn't hang out that long. I don't know if this was a general cultural difference.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and that people seem to be chilling a lot in San Diego on the beach.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You're in driving distance (in U.S. terms at least) to some of the most diverse and incredible nature in the world, and gas is so cheap compared to Denmark. Take advantage of this during your (hopefully) long weekends. Make some american friends on or off campus - it's easy and it makes the stay so much more fun and authentic. Sometimes you will feel lonely and miss your friends back home, sometimes it will be an administrative mess, but when you look back you will most likely look back at some of the best and most rewarding experiences in your life so far.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You definitely need a rental car for your whole stay. Dirt Cheap Car Rental which USD recommends are great and transparent.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Roadtripping in the incredible nature, and making real friends in the U.S. who e.g. took me to an american military base to play basketball, hosted an american "friendsgiving" and a halloween party, and surfing and playing beachvolleyball at the beach.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first few weeks craving friends while being stuck in a boring neighborhood far from the sea without a car to get around.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
